observation.visible_scene: A close-up kitchen shot: a person's hand grips a clear glass bowl tilted downward over a metal baking sheet lined with iridescent parchment paper. The bowl holds glossy melted dark chocolate, and a blue-handled spatula is held inside it. A continuous stream of chocolate drips from the bowl's lower rim onto a small rounded dollop already sitting on the parchment at the left-center of the tray. Background: tan stone-tile backsplash, speckled granite counter, a red lighter, a scale, and a glass measuring cup.
visible_changes: The hand and spatula make small, slow adjustments in angle and grip across the excerpt; the spatula tilts slightly more toward the bowl's rim over time, but the bowl's overall tilt stays roughly constant.
The chocolate stream from the rim to the parchment dollop persists throughout, with the swirl/streak pattern inside the bowl shifting subtly as chocolate moves.
The dollop on the parchment remains in the same position and looks roughly the same size, with the drip continually feeding it; no clear onset or completion of pouring is visible.
The background objects (lighter, scale, cup, tiles) hold their positions, indicating the camera is essentially static with at most negligible drift.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the chocolate dollop will become (e.g., a bark or drop) and any later steps.
How the bowl came to be tilted and dripping before frame 1.
Whether the dollop grows noticeably after the excerpt ends.
uncertain_details: Any measurable change in the dollop's size is too subtle to confirm from the frames.
Minor apparent shifts in framing could be small hand/bowl movement rather than camera motion.
